statement: For a specified pair of K-state CTMC probe matrices with permutation-orbit Frobenius gap gamma>0, unknown shared full-rank KxK column-stochastic emission matrix E with sigma_min(E)=kappa>0, fixed positive read duration Delta and conditionally independent outputs, and independent native founders with pi_i>=p_*>0, a calibrated positive-rate slow-read action can yield a finite-sample nearest-orbit test with error at most alpha using O(K/(p_* gamma^2) * kappa^-2 * polylog(K/(alpha p_* gamma))) reporter frames. All slow-block state-change probabilities, including ramps, must be union-bounded over the declared finite protocol, and the model order/candidate kernels are supplied.
novelty_boundary: Concentration and HMM identifiability are established prior art. This is a direct fixed-pair reconstruction with a paid positive slowdown and explicit ramp/jump accounting; priority and novelty are UNKNOWN. It is not general HMM identification.
costs: O(K gamma^-2 p_*^-1 log(K/alpha)) independent native founders for fixed confidence; O(K/(p_* gamma^2) kappa^-2 polylog) total reporter frames; R Delta plus measured ramps per block; nominal probe, detector, calibration, culture, viability, recovery, and actuator costs must be added.
falsifier: Reject or return UNKNOWN if the emission matrix changes across frames/actions, emissions are not conditionally independent, a jump/ramp envelope is unavailable or over budget, p_* is uncertified, the hardware rate floor blocks R, or gamma=0.
next_gate: Measure in a named target system the repeated-frame emission law and lower column-separation bound, initial-state occupancy lower bounds, complete hold/ramp transition-kernel bound, positive actuator floor, and total wall-time/exposure/viability costs.

statement: For the explicit uniform stationary three-state cycle pair and E_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)11^T/3, the fixed passive two-read pair law has KL D(J0||J1)=O(kappa^4), implying Omega(kappa^-4) independent pairs for any fixed testing error below one half even if E and pi are known.
novelty_boundary: This is the existing fixed pair-law baseline, not a lower bound for arbitrary passive trajectories or richer action suites.
costs: Two reporter reads per independent founder/pair; finite sample needs Omega(kappa^-4) pairs for fixed error; no physical unit prices supplied.
falsifier: An algebraic or numerical counterexample to the exact pair-law difference or KL asymptotic for the stated family.
next_gate: Compare with any proposed legal action under an explicitly matched sensor/action budget; do not elevate to a universal passive lower bound.

statement: Selected reversible cryo-arrest protocols support repeated imaging in particular living-cell molecular assays, but do not establish a uniform scalar slowdown Q->rho Q for arbitrary cell-fate labels or stable emission matrix E.
novelty_boundary: Physical feasibility is established only for protocol-specific imaging targets; the theorem-to-biology bridge is not claimed.
costs: Cooling/warming time, cryoprotectant/medium exchange, repeated frames, ramps, detector exposure, culture, viability, recovery, reporter calibration, and actuator calibration.
falsifier: Protocol-specific assays show an unbounded fate-state transition kernel, excess ramp disturbance, emission drift/bleaching, or cost/viability exceeding declared limits.
next_gate: Measure the exact action path, Q_F(t) confidence envelope, E_F across frames, no-jump bound, and all physical costs on the target state definition.
